reasons: The cited Section 12.3 is a genuine, mutual insurance regime covering commercial general liability, umbrella excess, clinical trials liability, professional liability for subcontractors and product liability, with A- rated insurers, additional-insured status, tail coverage, cancellation notice and certificates of insurance on request — this meets or exceeds the fallback and substantially the preferred position, so a 'compliant' classification is correct.

No redline or counterparty comment is proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; the deterministic check confirms an insurance obligation is present, so this is not a 'missing' clause case.

The rationale properly notes the shortfalls (redacted [***] limits that cannot be verified and no dedicated cyber/privacy line, with data handling addressed in Article 11) as minor sub-elements rather than flagging them as deviations, consistent with the classification guidance.
The obligation is mutual and confers benefit on our party as additional insured, so declining to redline avoids over-flagging a clause that benefits us.
